title: Whole Genre Sequencing
finding: Computational study applying weighted gene co-expression network analysis to ~1,400 Harlequin Presents novels (1999-2013); concludes the genre's architecture is a 'choir of authorial voices', its evolution shows sudden shifts linked to publisher financial pressures, and the order in which elements appear (the plot) is largely fixed (per author).
why_for_us: Empirical support that romance beats follow a stable order; we can borrow the fixed sequence of beats and spread it thinly, one beat per episode, without inventing a new structure.

title: Relational arcs as narrative structure: Dynamics, distribution and diachronic change in fiction
finding: Analysis of >120,000 automatically annotated character relationships in 96 novels (1850-1950): relationship trajectories form recurring arcs, e.g. conflicts peaking near the climax and romances resolving toward the end; arcs cluster into four shapes (Rise, U-shape, Decline, Oscillating) and genres leave distinct relational fingerprints (per authors).
why_for_us: Supports placing the romantic resolution (or its strongest beat) near the season end, after the legal-thriller climax, and using an oscillating or U-shaped romance arc rather than a straight rise.

title: A Natural History of the Romance Novel
finding: Book (genre history/theory): Regis argues that the romance novel, the most popular but least respected genre, does not enslave women but celebrates their freedom and joy, and offers critics an expanded vocabulary for discussing the genre (per OpenAlex abstract). The abstract does not list her eight essential elements.
why_for_us: The standard reference for romance beats (society, meeting, barrier, attraction, declaration, point of ritual death, recognition, betrothal); the beat list must be checked in the book itself before we map one beat per episode.

title: The final couple : happy endings in Hollywood cinema
finding: PhD thesis on the 'final couple' (ultimate romantic union) in Hollywood: the 'happy ending' is hard to define as a homogeneous norm, some films make the final couple feel emphatically closed while others render the same convention comparatively open, and happy endings are as open to variation as any other convention (per author).
why_for_us: Season 1 need not choose between a kiss and nothing: an 'open' final-couple ending (they agree to work one case together) gives closure for the season while keeping the slow burn alive.

title: Women Read the Romance: The Interaction of Text and Context
finding: Article on how romance texts and reading contexts interact; the available abstract only sets out the scale of the market (Harlequin claimed 168 million romances sold worldwide in 1979, per author) and notes that the audience's composition and size had not been accurately determined.
why_for_us: Background for treating romance as a reading practice tied to readers' lives; for a professional audience the context (the office, the deeds) is part of what makes the romance meaningful.

title: Genre, Gender and the Effects of Neoliberalism
finding: Book on new-millennium Hollywood romantic comedy: although critics dismiss the genre's strict, predictable formula, it has grown steadily over three decades; the book evaluates the structure of cycles such as teen romance, the new career woman, women as action heroes and the mature woman (per author).
why_for_us: The 'career woman' rom-com cycle is the closest film model for two apprentices competing professionally; predictability of the formula is not a commercial weakness.

title: Love is a Many-Person'd Thing: Multi-Protagonist Tales of Contemporary Desire
venue: RACO (Revistes Catalanes amb Accés Obert) (Consorci de Serveis Universitaris de Catalunya)
finding: Essay: combining the multi-protagonist form with romantic comedy produces portrayals of intimacy full of discordant voices, unlike romantic comedy's 'same old story', which the author argues calls for a broader, more flexible definition of the genre.
why_for_us: A romance woven among several office characters (notary, aunt, clients) is an established variant, so the couple need not carry every scene.

title: According to Their Plots, Jane Austen’s Novels Are Not Comic Romances with Happy Endings
finding: Computational affect study scoring Austen's six novels and Cinderella with the Dictionary of Affect: Cinderella is very pleasant with a distinct happy ending, whereas Emma, Pride and Prejudice and Northanger Abbey have equivocal endings, Mansfield Park and Sense and Sensibility relatively unpleasant ones, and Persuasion the least pleasant language overall but a happy ending (per author; regression and means comparisons).
why_for_us: Even canonical slow-burn romances do not climb steadily toward pleasantness; an emotionally muted tone with a late warm turn (Persuasion pattern) suits a restrained office romance.

title: Will they, won’t they? Dream sequences and virtual consummation in the series Moonlighting
finding: Essay: Moonlighting sustained the leads' sparring tension by offering regular dream/genre-pastiche sequences in which the couple 'consummated' the relationship, while deferring it in the diegesis; the brief period when they were actually a couple was met with general disappointment from fans and creators (per author).
why_for_us: A precedent for giving viewers 'almost' moments (imagined, hypothetical, or role-played closeness) without resolving the real relationship; in a notary office this could be a rehearsal of a client's vows or a mock signing rather than a real kiss.

title: The Temporality of (Serialized) Romantic Comedy
venue: Networking Knowledge Journal of the MeCCSA Postgraduate Network
finding: Essay: romantic comedies run on a 'temporality of the almost', a micro-narrative structure that repeatedly makes erotic resolution almost happen; the constant deferral looks like obstacles keeping the couple apart but in fact increases desire between characters and between narrative and spectators (per author).
why_for_us: Fits 'one emotional beat per episode': each 60-90 s episode can end on an 'almost' (a hand nearly touching over a document, an interrupted sentence) that raises desire without resolving it.

title: Will They or Won't They Couples Data
finding: Dataset/project description: IMDb viewer ratings scraped for 150 popular 'will they or won't they' couples from 125 TV series, modelled with an interrupted time series where the interruption is the couple's first kiss, to test whether ratings change on average after that milestone (per authors). The record describes the design, not the result.
why_for_us: The only quantitative handle on the 'first kiss' moment we found; it frames the first kiss as a measurable plot interruption, so we should decide deliberately which of the 8 episodes (if any) carries it.

title: For better or for worse: The “kiss effect” on television ratings
finding: Popular-statistics magazine article (Significance, RSS) presenting the IMDb ratings analysis of what happens to will-they-won't-they shows after the first kiss; the OpenAlex abstract is only a teaser and does not state the direction or size of the effect.
why_for_us: Directly addresses the 'Moonlighting curse' belief; until the full text is read we cannot claim either that the kiss hurts or helps, so do not plan the season around the curse myth.

title: Unsettling a sacred relationship: The mother–daughter–man romantic love triangle in telenovelas
finding: Multimethod (textual and ethnographic) study of three telenovelas: telenovelas are serialized love stories whose happy endings are postponed by intrigues and obstacles, and the love triangle is described as their basic building block; the risky mother-daughter-man triangle can succeed but poses writing and reception challenges (per author).
why_for_us: A third party is the classic serial postponement device; if used, a rival should come from the legal plot (e.g. a client or opposing lawyer) so it serves both threads, and family-loyalty triangles (the aunt) need careful handling.

title: The Essential Obstacle
finding: Screenwriting manual chapter: a love story needs an obstacle or opposing force keeping the two apart, something they must overcome, escape or endure; without it the love story will not work (per author).
why_for_us: Kuba and Zosia need one clear, legitimate obstacle (e.g. their offices represent opposite parties in the same transaction, or confidentiality rules) rather than vague hesitation.

title: 摯情解心結－電視劇《結婚好嗎？》逼顯主題的主要情節
finding: Analysis of the Taiwanese series Marry or Not: an absorbing main romance plot is built from two forces that attract yet exclude each other, pushed closer and pulled apart alternately, and can be organised through varied push-pull interaction patterns (per English abstract).
why_for_us: A simple episode grammar: alternate 'closer' and 'apart' beats across the 8 episodes so the single emotional beat per episode keeps changing direction.

title: Conflict Resolution in Love Triangles: Perspectives Offered by Chinese TV Dramas
finding: Study of Chinese television drama serials: social changes accompanying economic reform were presented as the main causes of love triangles, and conflicts were resolved mostly peacefully through conversations between rivals rather than confrontation, partly explained by rising tolerance for violating traditional relationship values (per authors).
why_for_us: A rival need not produce open confrontation; a calm, civil rivalry is a genre-consistent option that keeps the tone tasteful for a professional audience.

title: Challenging the Love Triangle in Twenty-First-Century Fantastic Young Adult Literature
venue: The International Journal of Young Adult Literature
finding: Essay: in 21st-century fantastic YA the love triangle is pervasive and its outcome rarely varies, with the heroine making a final choice between two suitors and inevitably disappointing readers who favoured the other; the author links resistance to alternative outcomes to market and reader anxieties.
why_for_us: A triangle forces a final choice that alienates part of the audience; for a subtle thread with one beat per episode, a triangle is probably more cost than benefit.

title: The trope enemies to lovers : an analysis of book lovers and love, theoretically
venue: Lume (Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul)
finding: Student thesis analysing the enemies-to-lovers trope in Emily Henry's Book Lovers (2022) and Ali Hazelwood's Love, Theoretically (2023) to describe its structure and narrative patterns, which the author says are used to appeal to a loyal audience.
why_for_us: Professional rivalry turning into respect is a recognised contemporary trope; two apprentices from competing offices fit it naturally.

title: Stuck on Repeat: Serial Time, Romantic Fatigue, and Netflix’s In Love All Over Again (2023)
venue: VIEW Journal of European Television History and Culture
finding: Case study (essay) of Netflix Spain's serialised romcom: stretching the will-they-won't-they dynamic over a serialised, non-linear structure first deepened romantic tension but the endless deferral became exhausting, draining narrative and erotic charge, a fatigue the author links to negative reception and rapid cancellation.
why_for_us: The counterweight to 'delay is good': deferral without progress tires viewers, so every episode must move the relationship one visible step even if consummation stays off-screen.

title: Media Portrayals of Romantic Relationship Maintenance: A Content Analysis of Relational Maintenance Behaviors on Prime-Time Television
finding: Content analysis of committed couples on prime-time network TV: the frequency of maintenance behaviours (positivity, understanding, self-disclosure, assurances, relationship talks, tasks, networks) varied by type, genre and couple type; comedies showed more maintenance behaviours, including more negative ones, than dramas; no sex differences (per authors).
why_for_us: Small concrete behaviours (sharing a task, a word of reassurance) are the currency of on-screen relationships; each episode's beat can be one such behaviour rather than a declaration.

title: Putting the Premium into Basic: Slow-Burn Narratives and the Loss-Leader Function of AMC’s Original Drama Series
finding: Narrative-industrial analysis of AMC (Mad Men, Breaking Bad, Rubicon) showing how a basic-cable economic model enabled deliberately paced 'slow-burn' storytelling within an advertiser-supported context (per author). Not about romance specifically.
why_for_us: 'Slow burn' is a business as well as an aesthetic choice; on a short-form platform that pays for completion and retention, the slow romance has to sit on top of a fast main plot rather than replace it.

title: The Structure of Family and Romantic Ties in the Soap Opera: An Ethnographic Approach
finding: Methodological article proposing to trace the kinship and romance structures among soap opera characters and to observe how the narrative activates this structure, as a way of revealing how a culture negotiates primordial relationships, power, genre and gender (per authors).
why_for_us: Treat the romance as part of a network (Zosia's aunt's office vs. Kuba's notary), so that legal conflicts between the offices automatically become romantic obstacles.

title: «Aber Liebe … ist nur eine Geschichte». Neurobiologische und psychologische Aspekte der Paarbeziehung im seriellen Erzählen am Beispiel der Krankenhausserien Grey’s Anatomy und In aller Freundschaft
finding: Book combining neurobiological and couple-psychology research with film analysis of couple relationships in serial storytelling in two hospital series, Grey's Anatomy and In aller Freundschaft (per abstract); the abstract does not state specific results.
why_for_us: The only work found that analyses couple arcs inside workplace procedurals; worth reading for how hospital series interleave cases and relationships.

title: Love stories
finding: Chapter on three British TV love-story serials by Jack Rosenthal, including The Lovers, whose comic effect rests on the young protagonists' unresolved courtship (per author).
why_for_us: A precedent for serial comedy built entirely on an unresolved courtship; gentle humour can carry the restraint.

title: Cultural Proximity and Genre Proximity: How Do Chinese Viewers Enjoy American and Korean TV Dramas?
finding: Quantitative content analysis of a probability sample of 16,440 viewer comments on 411 TV dramas: cultural proximity predicted involvement but not enjoyment; viewers enjoyed Korean dramas through involvement with characters and American dramas through involvement with the narrative; involvement differed by genre including romance (per authors).
why_for_us: K-drama-style romance works through attachment to characters, so the Kuba/Zosia thread should invest in small character moments while the legal plot supplies narrative drive, a split that matches the two routes found here.

title: The returning of Hallyu in China: transnational reception of the Korean drama My Love from the Star
finding: Textual analysis of 100 Douban reviews: urban middle-class Chinese viewers were attracted by the actors' beauty and the conservative romantic storyline and admired depicted pursuits of free love and career success, but criticised stereotypical gender relations and female submission (per author).
why_for_us: Conservative, restrained romance can attract an adult audience, but gender stereotypes are penalised; Zosia must be Kuba's professional equal, not a rescued heroine.

title: The Dilemmas of Modern Working Women in Hong Kong
finding: Interview study with 15 Korean TV drama fans (career women in Hong Kong): themes were psychological realism and 'Asian subtlety', workplace rationality vs. Chinese 'qing', conflicting discourses of femininity, and pleasure from vicarious romance and images of weak, crying men (per authors).
why_for_us: Working women valued subtlety and workplace realism in televised romance, close to our audience of office staff; emotional vulnerability from Kuba may land better than displays of confidence.

title: Korean TV drama viewership on Netflix: Transcultural affection, romance, and identities
venue: Journal of International and Intercultural Communication
finding: Analysis of Netflix reviews by US viewers: they engaged with Korean dramas through affective consumption tied to love themes, showing high emotional involvement in portrayed romantic feelings and characters' interactions and relating them to their own lives (per author).
why_for_us: K-drama romance travels through feelings and interactions rather than sex; small interactions between Kuba and Zosia can carry the thread for a non-Korean audience.

title: Dizis turcas: o romance, o sensorial e o erótico
finding: Essay: Turkish dizis are weekly serials with lengthy episodes told with unusual slowness and a particular emphasis on heterosexual romance; the article examines this slow pacing and the construction of a sensory and narrative eroticism characteristic of the format (per author).
why_for_us: Dizis show that eroticism can be built from looks, proximity and slowness instead of explicit contact; in 60-90 s, one slowed moment per episode can carry that charge.

title: Hybridity, Confucianism, and Ambiguity in the South Korean Soft Power Model in Hallyu 1.0
finding: Essay: K-drama narratives are commonly described as resting on Confucian and family values with a 'reserved romance' and conservativeness tied to 'soft masculinity'; the authors argue several of these elements (theme songs, reserved romance) mirror Western models and may not fully reflect Confucian claims.
why_for_us: 'Reserved romance' is a named, exportable convention rather than a purely cultural accident, so a restrained Polish thread can borrow it deliberately; treat claims about its Confucian roots with caution.

title: In Sickness and in Love? Autumn in My Heart and the Embodiment of Morality in Korean Television Drama
finding: Study combining analysis of the K-drama Autumn in My Heart (2000) with young Korean women's own love stories: the modern ideology of romantic love is a prominent K-drama theme, and informants framed their love stories through the dramas; the author argues about the melodramatic form that emerges (per author).
why_for_us: Melodramatic K-drama love is moral as well as emotional; Kuba and Zosia's choices about professional ethics can double as romantic tests.

title: K-Drama 2.0: updating tropes with intertextuality and cinematic visuals in Crash Landing on You
venue: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
finding: Essay: international SVOD entry into Korean broadcasting since 2016 changed K-drama's genres, quality and scale; the article examines how K-drama's representative romance genres evolved (updating tropes through intertextuality and cinematic visuals) in Crash Landing on You.
why_for_us: Old romance tropes can be refreshed by style and self-awareness; AI-generated visuals can quote K-drama looks (lingering glances, slow motion) while the story stays restrained.

title: The O of Han Ju
finding: Essay: one of the climaxes of Korean Wave dramas is the woman's confession of love to the man; the author argues such outbursts are contained by patriarchy, boosting a male ego that withholds affection until the woman confides first.
why_for_us: The confession is a recognisable climax beat; who confesses first is loaded, so letting Kuba be the more vulnerable one avoids the critique.

title: From Korean Wave to Korean Living: Meteor Garden and the Politics of Love Fantasies in Taiwan
venue: Korea Observer - Institute of Korean Studies
finding: Essay using the inter-Asian drama Meteor Garden (Boys Over Flowers) to examine how women's desire for love is formed; argues women's attachment to Korean dramas rests on a politics of recognition that essentialises and naturalises women's desire for love.
why_for_us: Cinderella/chaebol fantasy is powerful but politically criticised; a peer-level romance between two apprentices avoids the rich-saviour trope.

title: Articulating love: the narrative mechanisms and allegories of subjectivity in Chinese romance micro-dramas
finding: Essay on popular Chinese romantic costume micro-dramas: they share a transparent, familiar narrative pattern that lets audiences immerse themselves comfortably, follow the motif of 'quest-fulfillment', and offer a therapeutic emotional connection to love, without innovating on genre (per author).
why_for_us: Micro-drama romance relies on familiar, legible tropes; for a subtle thread we can keep the trope recognisable (rivals from two offices, slow trust) and spend originality on the notarial detail instead.

title: How Micro-Dramas Produce Emotional Value: An Archetypal Narrative Study of the “Wish-Fulfillment” Mechanism
finding: Content analysis with three-level coding of 100 popular micro-dramas: they build a 'wish-fulfillment' emotional mechanism from six event categories and seven image categories, characterised by abrupt plot reversals, high conflict density, extreme characterisation and fragmented viewing (per authors).
why_for_us: Shows what we are deliberately not doing: our romance thread is low-density and subtle, so the high-density hooks must come from the legal plot, not the couple.

title: Producing Commissioned Drama for Chinese Short Video Platforms: Power, Dependence and Creative Control
finding: Interview and industry-observation study of the Chinese micro-drama industry: micro dramas are a high-volume serial format with fast-paced episodes of a few minutes on online video platforms; the article maps production structures, power relations and creative control (per author).
why_for_us: Production context for 60-90 s episodes; platform dependence pushes toward formula, which our niche, professional audience may let us resist.

title: A New Research Programme for Reading Research: Analysing Comments in the Margins on Wattpad
venue: DigitCult - Scientific Journal on Digital Cultures
finding: Methods paper: Wattpad's comments in the margins let researchers compare specific text passages with their effects on readers; the authors outline a research programme combining reader-response theory, cognitive literary studies and computational text analysis (per authors).
why_for_us: Episode-level comments are a usable feedback signal; we can track which romance beats viewers comment on and adjust season 2.

title: Webtoon Romance Reading and New Ways to Look at Genre Reading
finding: Semistructured interviews with 16 readers of both webtoon romance and romance novels: immersive engagement enabled by multimedia devices, platform accessibility and diversity in romance narratives were the main appeals of webtoon romance (per authors).
why_for_us: Serial visual romance on phones is appreciated for immersion and convenience; vertical video can exploit the same immersion with close framing.

title: What Outfit Shall the Protagonist Wear? New models of revenue creation in online fiction platforms
finding: Analysis of online fiction platforms (Wattpad, Tapas, Choices, Episode): free-to-read models monetise narrative through ad-supported serialization and paywalls, and some platforms offer readers paid choices within stories (per author).
why_for_us: Romance serials are monetised at episode boundaries; if the series is ever paywalled, the romance beat is a natural episode-end pull, but not at the cost of subtlety.

title: “Ilysm!” Serial Writing and Social Reading on Wattpad
finding: Chapter examining serial writing and social reading on Wattpad through Jenkins' participatory culture and Kelleter's theory of serial storytelling, analysing the social interaction in and around two serial stories (per author).
why_for_us: Serial romance is co-produced with its audience's reactions; a short-form series can plan room for audience feedback between seasons.

title: Mass-produced romance: BookTok society and the homogenisation of literary culture
venue: Jurnal Studi Komunikasi (Indonesian Journal of Communications Studies)
finding: Study applying Adorno's culture-industry concept to argue that BookTok reinforces literary homogenisation through algorithm-driven virality of romance titles (per author; abstract truncated in our record).
why_for_us: Trope-driven romance spreads well on short video but risks sameness; a notary setting is our differentiator.

title: Beyond Pleasure: Exploring the Eudaimonic Entertainment Experience
finding: Two studies; in one, a film's ending was manipulated (sad vs. happy): hedonic entertainment measures were affected by the ending manipulation, whereas the new five-dimension eudaimonic (meaningfulness) measures were not (per authors).
why_for_us: A sad or open season ending lowers pleasure but not meaningfulness, so a bittersweet season-1 finale for Kuba and Zosia is defensible if the series wants depth, while a happier beat keeps hedonic enjoyment.

title: Exploring the Paradox of the Enjoyment of Sad Films
finding: Three studies on 'meta-emotions': sad reactions to sad films were positively related to enjoyment, females reported stronger sadness and enjoyment than males, and the Sad-Film Scale correlated with empathy, femininity and positive appraisal of sad emotions and predicted enjoyment of a specific sad film (per author).
why_for_us: Melancholy and longing can be enjoyed in themselves, so an unresolved, wistful beat is not a failure; the effect may be stronger for the largely female office staff audience.

title: Why we like to watch sad films. The pleasure of being moved in aesthetic experiences.
venue: Psychology of Aesthetics Creativity and the Arts
finding: Cinema study using sadness-eliciting film clips, proposing that the feeling of being moved explains how sadness can coexist with aesthetic liking and pleasure (per authors; abstract truncated in our record).
why_for_us: Aim the romance beats at 'being moved' (small kindness, sacrifice for the other's career) rather than at excitement.

title: Tragedy Viewers Count Their Blessings: Feeling Low on Fiction Leads to Feeling High on Life
finding: Participants (n=361) watched a tragedy: greater sadness led to greater enjoyment, mediated by life reflection through self- and socially focused thoughts (per authors).
why_for_us: A sad turn in the romance (e.g. one apprentice leaving) can increase enjoyment if it prompts reflection on viewers' own relationships at work.

title: Tender Affective States as Predictors of Entertainment Preference
finding: Four studies: tenderness (warmth, sympathy, understanding) was associated with greater interest in sad films and with preferences for entertainment featuring drama and human connection (per author).
why_for_us: Tenderness, not passion, is the target affect for a 'tasteful' thread; scenes of care and understanding should dominate.

title: “The vile conclusion”. Crises of resolution in Shakespeare's love plots
finding: Essay applying Peter Brooks' narrative dynamics: plot and resolution are dueling forces throughout a story, one complicating and sustaining it, the other resolving it; the article reads Shakespeare's romantic love plots through this tension (per author).
why_for_us: Resolution is a force that ends the story; keep resolution pressure visible but always counterweighted by a new complication from the legal plot.

title: Love interests
finding: Screenwriting guide chapter: the love interest is often the most poorly written character in non-romance scripts while being most important in purpose; the purpose is not simply to add romance and can be achieved without romance or sex (per author).
why_for_us: Zosia must have a story function in the legal plot (ally, mirror, obstacle), not decorative romance; that is also what keeps the thread from distracting.

title: Doubled Plots: Romance and History
finding: Edited essay collection examining how romance (associated with emotions and private life) and history (public events) parallel and reflect each other when doubled within narratives (per abstract).
why_for_us: Frames the core design: the private plot (Kuba-Zosia) should mirror the public/legal plot thematically (trust, signatures, binding promises).

title: Mystery and the Romance Reader
finding: Librarianship article: mystery and romance share many elements and often the same readers; romance readers read widely and mystery readers often enjoy romantic suspense, and authors such as Janet Evanovich combine both genres to please large readerships (per author).
why_for_us: Supports the hybrid: a romance thread can widen the appeal of a mystery/procedural to readers who come for the relationship.

title: A linguagem cifrada de Eros: suspense, comédia romântica e Você
venue: Zanzalá - Revista Brasileira de Estudos de Ficção Científica
finding: Essay on the series You, which mixes suspense thriller and romantic comedy and draws an ambivalent audience response; argues the two genres share narrative tension, suspense and eroticism (per author).
why_for_us: Thriller suspense and romantic suspense run on the same engine, so legal-plot cliffhangers and romantic 'almosts' can be timed together.

title: Brienne of Tarth and Jaime Lannister: A Romantic Comedy Within HBO's Game of Thrones
venue: Mythlore: A Journal of J.R.R. Tolkien, C.S. Lewis, Charles Williams, and Mythopoeic Literature
finding: Essay arguing that HBO's Game of Thrones reveals characters mainly through odd-couple relationships and that the Brienne-Jaime pairing functions as a romantic comedy embedded within the epic (per author).
why_for_us: Romantic-comedy structure can be nested inside a darker genre through one odd-couple pairing, which is the role Kuba and Zosia play inside the legal thriller.

title: Love and detection nel noir americano
venue: IRIS Research product catalog (Sapienza University of Rome)
finding: Book chapter analysing couple dynamics in crime investigations across a sample of American police sagas of the late 20th century; although sometimes relegated to a secondary role, the woman often proves sharper than her male partner (per abstract).
why_for_us: Investigating couples are a long-standing crime convention; let Zosia solve the key notarial detail, making the romance part of the detection.

title: Romancing the Past: History, Love, and Genre in Vincent Ward's River Queen
finding: Essay: in River Queen (2005) romance complicates and extends a historical narrative of colonial violence; romance glamorizes history but is also a complex, hybrid generic element (per author).
why_for_us: Romance makes a serious frame more accessible but can 'glamorize' it; keep notarial procedure accurate so the romance does not trivialise the legal stakes.
